entities.summary: Jean Bodman Fletcher was a pioneering American architect whose career reshaped modern residential and institutional design. As a founding member of The Architects' Collaborative (TAC) in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Fletcher broke gender barriers in a male-dominated field and introduced innovative design concepts that addressed the postwar demand for livable, efficient, and community-oriented spaces. Her work not only revolutionized architectural practice through a collaborative model but also continues to influence contemporary design through its emphasis on functionality and human-centered planning.
